simple: This page explains the building blocks Roblox uses to play sound. Each audio object acts like a real piece of sound gear: a music player, a speaker, a microphone, or a cable. You connect them with `Wire` objects to make sound play everywhere (2D audio) or from a spot in the world (3D audio). It also covers turning text into a spoken voice and turning a player's speech into text.
analogy: It is like hooking up a home stereo. The `AudioPlayer` is the music player, the `Wire` is the cable, and the `AudioDeviceOutput` is your headphones. Unplug the cable and you hear nothing.
keyPoints: Audio objects either make sound (like `AudioPlayer`), receive it (like `AudioEmitter`), change it (effects), or carry it (`Wire`).
2D audio needs three objects in SoundService: an `AudioPlayer`, an `AudioDeviceOutput`, and a `Wire` from the player to the output.
A `Wire` uses `SourceInstance` for where the sound comes from and `TargetInstance` for where it goes.
3D audio puts an `AudioPlayer`, an `AudioEmitter`, and a `Wire` inside a part, and SoundService's `ListenerLocation` (Character or Camera) creates the listener and output for you.
`DistanceAttenuation` on an `AudioEmitter` is a curve that sets how loud the sound is at each distance.
`AudioTextToSpeech` reads text out loud (up to 300 characters) using a voice picked by `VoiceId`.
`AudioSpeechToText` turns microphone speech into text; you wire an `AudioDeviceInput` into it and set its `Player`.
To start a sound from code, call `:Play()` on an `AudioPlayer` that is wired up correctly.

terms.2D audio: Sound with no location. It is the same volume wherever your character stands, like background music.
terms.3D audio: Sound that comes from a place in the world. Stand 5 studs from a radio and it is loud; stand 100 studs away and it is quiet or silent.
terms.audio stream: The sound flowing from one audio object to the next through wires.
terms.AudioEmitter: A pretend speaker. It sends sound out from the position of whatever it is parented to, such as a part.
terms.AudioListener: A pretend microphone, usually on the camera or the player's character, that picks up sound from emitters nearby.
terms.AudioDeviceOutput: Stands for the player's real speakers or headphones. Sound must reach this to be heard.
terms.SourceInstance / TargetInstance: The two ends of a `Wire`. Source is where the sound starts, Target is where it goes. Example: Source = AudioPlayer, Target = AudioDeviceOutput.
terms.ListenerLocation: A SoundService setting that decides where the automatic listener goes: on the Camera, on the Character, or nowhere (None).
terms.DistanceAttenuation: A volume-over-distance curve. The page's example plays at half volume at 50 studs away and drops to silent at 70 studs.
terms.attenuation: Sound getting quieter, usually because you are farther away.
terms.amplitude / Volume: How loud the sound is. `AudioPlayer.Volume` goes from 0 (silent) to 10.
terms.Looping: When on, the sound starts over each time it ends, like music that never stops.
terms.text-to-speech (TTS): The computer reads written words out loud with an artificial voice.
terms.speech-to-text (STT): The computer listens to someone talking and writes down the words.
terms.VoiceId: A number that picks the TTS voice. For example 1 is British male and 4 is United States female #1.
terms.tokenize: Breaking a sentence into a list of single words, for example "Open the door!" becomes `open`, `the`, `door`.

example.title: Play background music for everyone
example.code:
local SoundService = game:GetService("SoundService")

-- The audio player loads and plays the sound file
local player = Instance.new("AudioPlayer")
player.Asset = "rbxassetid://1234567890" -- replace with your own audio asset ID
player.Looping = true -- start over when it ends
player.Volume = 1
player.Parent = SoundService

-- The output stands for everyone's speakers or headphones
local output = Instance.new("AudioDeviceOutput")
output.Parent = SoundService

-- The wire carries sound from the player to the output
local wire = Instance.new("Wire")
wire.SourceInstance = player
wire.TargetInstance = output
wire.Parent = SoundService

-- Wait until the sound file is loaded, then play it
while not player.IsReady do
	task.wait(0.1)
end
player:Play()
explain: We get SoundService, the usual home for sounds that play everywhere.
We make an `AudioPlayer` and give it an asset ID, turn on looping, and set the volume.
We make an `AudioDeviceOutput`. Because we do not set its `Player`, everyone hears it.
We make a `Wire` and set `SourceInstance` to the player and `TargetInstance` to the output, which connects them.
We wait until `IsReady` is true so the file is loaded, then call `:Play()`.

watchOut: No sound? Check the `Wire`. If `SourceInstance` or `TargetInstance` is empty or pointing at the wrong object, nothing is heard.
For 3D sound you need two wires: player to emitter, and listener to output. Setting `ListenerLocation` to Character or Camera makes the second half for you.
If your 3D sound cuts out too soon, look at the `DistanceAttenuation` curve; it may drop to zero at a short distance.
Text-to-speech text is limited to 300 characters and must follow Roblox's Community Standards.
Turning on the microphone for speech-to-text also turns on voice chat by default. Turn off `EnableDefaultVoice` on VoiceChatService if you do not want others to hear players.
